messages.subject: Re: error message for Msstats QC in Skyline
messages.subject_clean: error message for Msstats QC in Skyline
messages.body_plain:
Dear Xi,

MSstats requires that for each feature the input file contains one line for every run (i.e., the total # of lines in the input file is # of features x # of runs). If a peak is missing in a run, its intensity should be denoted as 'NA'. The log file indicates that this is not the case for your input data. If you are using MSstats with Skyline, you should go back to Skyline and make sure that all the peaks are selected in all the runs. If you use MSstats in R with the command line, you can edit the input file. Finally, in MSstats it is possible to replace "fillIncompleteRows = FALSE" with "fillIncompleteRows = TRUE". In this case, MSstats will try to guess the location of the missing peaks and fill in the lines automatically. However I suggest that you use this option with caution, because we cannot guarantee that the guess is correct. It is always best to go to the raw data, and make sure that the data are red correctly.

Sincerely
Olga

messages.subject: Analysiing factorial designed experimental data
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have been using the Msstats package in R version 3.1.0 to compare protein abundances between two conditions. Now I want to compare  the protein abundance in multiple level of variables from a factorial designed experiment, perhaps using ANOVA. I have tried the multiple comparison using the “rbind” function but I think it still compares between two condition? Is there any ways that I can use to do analysis like 2-way  or 3-way ANOVA using MSstats?

messages.subject: Re: Analysiing factorial designed experimental data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Hafiz,

MSstats works with an arbitrary number of conditions, and with both crossed and nested factors. The limitation is that it only implements pairwise comparisons of the conditions (e.g., if you have 3 conditions, you can compare cond1 vs cond2, cond2 vs cond3, and cond1 vs cond3). Global comparisons of all the levels of a condition (e.g. with F-test) are currently not implemented, but this is on our todo list.

Sincerely
Olga
